value.text:
Skip to content
DEADBOARD
Bench Faults Boards Challenges Mods
Open the bench

> board-level repair trainer

Bring dead boards back.

DEADBOARD is a repair bench in your browser. Probe a real open-hardware board with a multimeter, read boot current off the bench supply, scope the switch nodes, find the short with a thermal camera, then fix it with an iron that obeys physics.

Open the bench → Learn the basics · 5 min

Runs in Chrome or Edge 113+, Safari 26+ (WebGPU). Nothing to install.

$ power on --supply 30V --rail 30V_GATE
G3H   standby .....................  0.0 mA
seq   S5 → S4 → S3 → S0 ...........  0.0 mA
S0    +5V +3V3 +1V2 up ............ 10.3 mA
S0    loads settle ................ 16.2 mA
ok    board alive

That's the board above, powering up on the bench (its rail names carry no power states, so every converter starts at S0). A stuck rail stalls the sequence. A short makes it loop.

> the bench

Instruments that behave like instruments.

Every tool a technician reaches for, with the same quirks and the same limits.

Multimeter

A 6000-count meter, not an ideal probe: 10 MΩ input, contact resistance, diode test. Capacitance reads high in circuit. The 10 A input only works in series.

Bench supply

Boot current you can read: standby, sleep, running. Current limit, and voltage injection to make the culprit on a shorted rail heat up.

Oscilloscope

Roll through power-up ramps and boot loops. Catch a switch node, its ripple, or a clock that never started.

Thermal camera

IR that reads like IR: bare solder looks cold. Freeze spray, isopropyl and the rosin method to pin the hot part.

Rework

Iron, hot air, preheater. Flux matters, ground pads fight back, and pads lift if you cook them.

Boardview

Both sides, 2D or a full 3D orbit. Click a part to see where its nets go. Search hundreds of parts in a keystroke.

> the faults

Boards fail the way real boards fail.

Not "part missing, find it". Faults come with realistic severity and realistic symptoms. Some only show up when the board is warm, or when you press on it.

  • dead-short MLCC
  • leaky capacitor
  • liquid residue
  • corroded copper
  • chip shorted inside
  • dead regulator
  • drifted resistor
  • resistive cold joint
  • opens when warm
  • works only when pressed
  • leaks when warm
  • lifted pad
  • cracked by thermal shock
  • reversed part

> real boards

Any board. No per-board scripting.

Import a boardview (.brd) or a KiCad layout. DEADBOARD finds the power tree, the regulators and the power states from the netlist and its net names, then simulates the whole board with a SPICE engine. Export it as an ngspice netlist whenever you like.

Made something? Package your boards, their BOM and schematic as a mod that anyone can install.

> honest simulation

Every number has a source.

Values come from the board data, datasheets and design intent. Where none exist, the estimate is labelled as an estimate, and synthesized waveforms say so on the scope. Measured a real board? Feed the readings back and DEADBOARD calibrates its model against your bench.

> challenges

Break it. Lock a flag. Share the link.

Start from a working board, plant faults, and lock a flag to the repaired circuit. The flag is encrypted with the board's topology, so only a real repair unlocks it. There's no peeking and no shortcut. Share it as a file or a single link. 

$ verify
✗ V(TP1) = 0.42 V   expected 2.30–2.70 V
✗ D1 is OFF          expected ON
# …swap R2 for 10 kΩ, bridge the broken bottom trace…
$ verify
✓ all checks green
✓ flag captured: PCB{…}

There's a dead board on the bench.

limitations: Event sequence records provider receipt order; simultaneous browser causality is not inferred.
Network content is retained only when selected; Playwright response-body bytes are API results and are not guaranteed to match wire bytes.
Request bytes are limited to what Playwright exposes; not_exposed does not establish body absence or multipart file coverage.
Network content reads settle within 5 seconds each and the observer does not request bodies from unfinished responses.

Captured response-body bytes are the result of Playwright's Response.body() API. Playwright may satisfy that API with a credentialed follow-up load of the request URL when CDP has no body, so transaction and event links do not verify that retained bytes came from the original network transaction.
Playwright scenario events do not expose request initiator stacks; receipt order does not prove causality.
Storage values are hashed only after declared-secret redaction.
